system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 3.4 already gives Bluefly a Customer-only convenience right (Agreement or any Service Option Attachment) on one month's notice, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right — both better than our fallback. The one material failure is Section 3.4(b)'s open-ended early termination charges, cross-referring to Attachment A and Service Option Attachments that IBM can unilaterally change under 13.1. messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Deterministic failures:
- Customer convenience termination present: failed

Verifier reasons:
- Fallback checklist is complete after the edit: the Customer convenience right (one month's notice, better than 60–90 days) and the absence of any Vendor mid-term convenience right were already met, and the single gap — open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and Service Option Attachments — is closed by the added cap "not to exceed three (3) months' charges."
- Preferred is not complete solely because there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer's convenience termination; to reach preferred the drafter would need to insert an express obligation that IBM refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination, pro rata.
- Minimal: the redline adds only the eight-word cap to Section 3.4(b), leaves the favourable one-month notice, the end-of-calendar-month mechanic, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out and the "if any" qualifier intact, and adds no survival, expense, refund or procedural extras outside the fallback checklist.
- Preserves intent: the cap attaches to the existing charge mechanic without creating undefined terms or dangling cross-references; Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments continue to govern which charges apply, now subject to a ceiling. Minor drafting note (not a defect): "three (3) months' charges" does not state the measurement base, so consider "three (3) months' recurring charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment" if IBM pushes back on ambiguity.
- Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is inconsistent with the text and should be treated as a regex artefact; the operative sentence does grant Customer the convenience right, so it does not undermine the finding.
- Classification as a deviation is supportable because an uncapped early-termination charge is a material failure of the fallback fee cap; the rationale correctly states the clause otherwise sits at (indeed above) the fallback and routes the 3.2 non-renewal mechanic to RENEWAL rather than double-flagging it here.

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Only Type I Materials vest in Customer ("Type I Materials are those ... in which Customer will have all right, title, and interest"); the retained Type II category covers Materials "created during the Service performance period or otherwise" in which "IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest", so deliverables generally are not Customer-owned.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered §7; Type I ownership is stated as a vesting/classification, and Type II expressly remains with IBM. No 'IBM assigns' operative wording was added.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Type II Materials expressly include those that "preexist the Service" and IBM or third parties retain "all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: As redlined: "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up, royalty-free license ... of Type II Materials" — Type II being the IBM-owned IP delivered to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up, royalty-free license" over Type II (IBM-owned) Materials.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Licence is expressly "paid-up, royalty-free" in the redlined §7.c.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No operative sentence states that Customer owns or retains all rights in Customer Data; §14.18 as redlined only constrains IBM's processing purpose, and §14.17 ("No other licenses or rights ... are granted") is not an ownership statement. A Customer Data ownership sentence must be inserted.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18: "Such information, and all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, will be processed solely to provide the Services", replacing the contractor/Business Partner/assignee promotions and marketing-research uses.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the Materials regime allocates title exclusively to either Customer (Type I) or IBM/third parties (Type II); no joint-ownership language exists to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7.c grants a "perpetual" licence over Type II Materials; the previous grant had no term word. Type I Materials are Customer-owned outright, so no licence is needed there.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "irrevocable" retained in the redlined §7.c grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" retained, and the countervailing restriction "within Customer's Enterprise only" has been removed from the grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "paid-up, royalty-free" in the redlined grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, distribute and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business" — modification right added and the Enterprise-only field limit deleted.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business"; §14.17's no-implied-licence sentence does not cut back an expressly specified licence.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18 confines IBM to processing contact information "and all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer ... solely to provide the Services"; the distribution to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for promotions and marketing research is deleted.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: every fallback element is met in operative language — Type II ownership left with IBM, and the §7.c grant now reads perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up/royalty-free, with modification and sublicensing for Customer's business, the Enterprise-only field limit having been removed as directly contradictory to those rights.

The Customer Data element is satisfied in substance: the purpose limitation covers not only contact information but "all other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer", and the independent-exploitation uses (contractors, Business Partners, assignees, promotions, marketing research) are struck, so no broad Vendor exploitation right survives.

Preferred remains incomplete for two specific defects the drafter would need to repair to reach that level: (i) no assignment operative language — insert an express 'IBM assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and work product created for Customer' and reverse the Type II default so Materials created for Customer are not classified as IBM-owned by default; and (ii) no Customer Data ownership sentence — insert 'As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data.'

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the §7.c licence verbs/qualifiers and the §14.18 purpose sentence. Retained favourable wording ('irrevocable', 'nonexclusive', 'worldwide', 'paid-up') is preserved, the Type I licence back to IBM in §7.b is untouched, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate is added. Adding 'royalty-free' alongside the retained 'paid-up' is checklist-required wording rather than gratuitous duplication.

Intent is preserved: §14.17's no-implied-licence rule still functions because the expanded grant is expressly specified; the retained sentence that contact information is not personal information processed on Customer's behalf addresses controller status and does not contradict the new purpose limitation; no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling.
Not walk-away territory: no assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to IBM is created, and no joint ownership is introduced.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term"), and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied: the opt-out window is 60 (not ≤30) days, no Vendor reminder is added, the renewal term is not fixed at ≤12 months, and the uplift cap is 105% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language ties each renewal to "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term," so a Service Option Attachment with an initial term longer than 12 months renews for that longer period; no 12-month ceiling was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Redline sets notice at "at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term," which exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 3.2 as amended imposes only a mutual notice right, not an IBM pre-renewal reminder.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap is "will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term" — a flat 5% ceiling with no CPI comparator or 3% limit.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 3.2 reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term." The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern artefact (the clause uses plain figures "60" rather than the document's "sixty (60)" convention); on substance the window is exactly 60 days and within the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "Charges for each renewal term will not exceed 105% of the charges in effect for the immediately preceding term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — an express 5% ceiling on renewal-term charges.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the non-renewal window is reduced from 90 to 60 days and renewal charges are capped at 105% of the prior term. The finding's 'deviation' classification and fallback targeting are correct, since the original 90-day window and uncapped renewal pricing both failed the fallback.

Preferred level fails on four counts, correctly noted rather than redlined: renewal term is still 'equal in duration to the previous term' (no 12-month cap), opt-out is 60 not 30 days, there is no IBM 60-day reminder, and the uplift cap is 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Minimality holds: only the notice figure was changed and one short cap sentence added; Section 13.1's mid-term change right, non-retroactivity and Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election are retained verbatim, and no unrelated words were deleted.
Drafting nit for the drafter (not a defect): conform the inserted figure to the document's convention — 'sixty (60) days' — so the number matches surrounding usage and passes automated term checks.

Residual risk to flag to the client, not a checklist failure: Section 13.1 still lets IBM change Service Option Attachment prices on 90 days' notice with no percentage limit; because the new cap is measured against 'charges in effect for the immediately preceding term,' a mid-term 13.1 increase resets the baseline. If we want the 5% ceiling to be airtight, add 'notwithstanding Section 13.1' or measure the cap against charges in effect on the applicable Service Option Attachment Start Date — but Customer's 30-day no-charge termination election under 13.1 mitigates this, so the current edit remains defensible as-is.

Also consider asymmetric drafting: the mutual 60-day figure shortens IBM's own non-renewal notice from 90 to 60 days, reducing Customer's warning of an IBM exit. Preserving 90 days for IBM while cutting Customer's window to 60 would be strictly more protective, though the single-number edit is the simpler minimal change.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.",
  "If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.",
  "If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.",
  "If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.",
  "If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.",
  "If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent."
]

Planner evidence and hints:
{"ruleId":"RENEWAL","candidateSectionIds":["sec-3.2","sec-3.1"],"candidateParagraphIds":[],"likelyAbsent":false,"note":"3.2 Renewal — test for automatic renewal, length of renewal term, the non-renewal notice window and any uplift/repricing mechanic; read with the initial term in 3.1."}

Before drafting an actionable proposal, call lookup_precedent. Treat returned approved language as an element-marked template, adapt it to this contract, and verify every marker; do not copy non-element extras.

Investigate every responsive location, choose one target level, validate the smallest complete proposal, map every target element, and submit one finding.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted text reads "no more than once per year"; "per year" (readable as calendar year) is not the same as "once in any 12-month period" and would permit back-to-back investigations in December and January.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Insertion gives "at least fifteen (15) days' notice" (and does not require it to be written); the preferred 30-day written standard is not pursued.

elements.element: Audits occur during business hours.
elements.evidence: No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in the rendered 11.3 language.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The investigation remains one IBM conducts itself ("IBM may investigate potential violations"); no independent auditor is required.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No auditor confidentiality undertaking is added; no auditor is specified at all.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference language in the insertion or retained paragraphs.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Insertion sets the cost-shift threshold at "underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%)", the fallback figure, not 5 percent.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Nothing in 11.3 grants IBM access to Customer systems; p0138 only obliges Customer to "provide all relevant information ... at IBM's request", i.e. information delivery rather than direct or remote system access, and the redline adds no access right.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "IBM may investigate potential violations under this Subsection 11.3 no more than once per year".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: "and only after giving Customer at least fifteen (15) days' notice" — a hard condition precedent on the investigation right, distinct from the softer "attempt to notify" in the retained p0137, which governs only the 11.3(a)/(b) enforcement activities.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "IBM will bear the costs of each such investigation unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%)."

reasons: All three fallback elements are met in operative language by a single inserted sentence pair; the fallback level is position-complete, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback.

Preferred level fails on six elements (30-day written notice, business hours, independent auditor, auditor confidentiality, off-site conduct, 5% cost-shift threshold) and on the "any 12-month period" formulation; the drafter deliberately elected the fallback, which is consistent with the deviation finding.

If the preferred position were later pursued, the exact repairs are: change "once per year" to "once in any twelve (12) month period", "fifteen (15) days' notice" to "thirty (30) days' prior written notice", add "during Customer's normal business hours", require "an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations", add "off-site wherever practicable", and reduce the threshold to five percent (5%).

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no favourable retained language (including the p0137 notice attempt and the emergency carve-out, which is confined to 11.3(a)/(b) activities) is disturbed, and the insertion adds no requirement outside the fallback checklist — no survival tail, expense allocation, records-retention or procedural extras.

Intent is preserved: the new sentence is scoped to "this Subsection 11.3", leaves p0132's investigation trigger, the 11.3(a)/(b) remedies and p0138's information-provision duty intact, and creates no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence.

Note for the drafter (not a defect at this level): the 10% "underpayment" cost trigger is imported from the payment-verification playbook and has no natural application to an AUP-compliance investigation, so in practice IBM will always bear the cost — a Customer-favourable outcome, but consider aligning the trigger to "a material breach of Subsection 11.2(b)" if you want the exception to have real content.
The pre-redline clause was correctly treated as a deviation: unlimited, unannounced investigation with no cost allocation sits in walk-away territory under this rule.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM / Vendor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]
