Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at any time by: a. providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM". The element is disjunctive and Agreement-level convenience termination is expressly granted; Service Option Attachments are this contract's order-level documents (referenced in the Order Forms per the resolved definition), so document-level partial exit is also preserved. The prerequisite-attachment carve-out is pre-existing language and does not negate the right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The month-end restriction was replaced with "for convenience at any time" and the notice changed from "at least one month's" to "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice". With the calendar-month-end trigger removed, the effective date is now a straight 30 days from notice, so nothing pushes the exit beyond 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "In the event of a termination by Customer for convenience under this Section 3.4, IBM will refund to Customer, pro rata, any prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely period-based), is owed by Vendor, and is triggered by Customer's 3.4 convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 3.3 gives IBM a mid-term exit only "for material breach of this Agreement by the other upon written notice" with a cure period; no clause in the operative text confers a Vendor no-cause exit. The only other IBM exit identified is the 90-day non-renewal notice in 3.2, which under the rule boundaries is assessed under RENEWAL as natural-term non-renewal, not as mid-term termination for convenience. Element already met; no edit required.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered notice is "at least thirty (30) days'", below the 60–90 day fallback band. (This is a Customer-favourable shortfall and is irrelevant because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 3.4(b) is retained verbatim and uncapped: "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments." No three-months-of-charges ceiling appears in operative language; the cap is only promised in the rationale as a fallback trade.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition satisfied a fortiori: IBM has no convenience termination right at all in the operative text (3.3 is breach-only), so there is no Vendor no-cause exit that could occur mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose stated condition does not apply: IBM holds no convenience termination right in the rendered text, so no Vendor convenience-notice period is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: the four preferred elements are met by three surgical edits plus one already-met element, so the position is position-complete at the preferred level.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" reporting false is a false negative on substance: the rendered clause reads "Customer may terminate this Agreement ... for convenience at any time by: a. providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM", which plainly grants the right. The other gates (three operations applying, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with the rendered text.

Minimality holds. Only three targeted changes were made — the month-end trigger became "at any time" (needed so the 30-day cap is not extended by up to a further month), "one month's" became "thirty (30) days'" (needed because one month can exceed 30 days), and a single-sentence pro-rata refund was inserted. Favourable retained language survives verbatim: the prerequisite-attachment carve-out, "if any" in 3.4(b), the continuing-performance sentence, and 3.3's bar on IBM recovering 3.4(b) charges after its own breach. No survival tail, expense language, damages categories, or "in whole or in part" surplus was added.

Intent is preserved: the refund sentence uses the same "effective date of termination" anchor, the continuing-performance sentence's reference to the "final termination date" remains coherent, and 3.3's cross-reference to Section 3.4(b) is intact because 3.4(b) was left untouched. No undefined term or dangling reference is created.

Repair note for the fallback path only: to make the fallback level complete the drafter must add an express operative cap in 3.4(b) (e.g. "which charges shall not in the aggregate exceed three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services") and move Customer notice into the 60–90 day band. As drafted the cap exists only in the margin rationale, which does not count as operative language.

Standing exposure to note in the rationale (not a checklist failure): retained 3.4(b) leaves early-termination charges open-ended by reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments. That is not one of the preferred atomic elements, so it cannot be inferred as an omitted element, but it partially offsets the newly added refund and should be flagged commercially.

Severity: the original clause already gave Customer a one-month convenience exit and gave IBM no convenience right at all, so this is well clear of walk-away territory; the live gaps were the month-end delay, the absent refund, and uncapped exit charges. Medium is the proportionate severity.

system.text:
You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-fee65dd5","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.1 Indemnification by IBM","rationale":"Section 8.1 sits at (and in one respect above) the INDEMN fallback. IBM defends and indemnifies Customer and its Enterprise against third-party claims that Materials or Base Components IBM provides or uses in performing the Services infringe patent, trademark, copyright or trade secret rights (p0089), with the usual permitted exclusions for Customer-supplied items incorporated into the Materials, Customer modifications and Customer combinations (p0092, p0093, p0095), and the procure-continued-use / modify / replace remedies plus a credit of amounts paid up to twelve months of applicable charges if none is reasonably available (p0091). On the fallback super-cap element, Section 9.1(a) carves indemnification payments under Section 8.1 out of IBM's damages cap entirely (p0110), so the indemnity is not limited to 3x annual fees — better than the fallback and not something we would redline. Standard procedure (prompt written notice, IBM control of the defence, Customer cooperation with reimbursement of cooperation costs) is present at p0090–p0091. Preferred-position gaps remain but are noted rather than flagged: no express cover for IBM's breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and Customer's indemnity in Section 8.2 is broader than Customer content and Customer's breach of law (notably Services Recipient claims), although Section 8.2(c) relieves Customer to the extent IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach caused the loss. If the deal allows a further ask, we would add IBM cover for breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct and trim Section 8.2(a)(3).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-67988114","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.10 Assignment","rationale":"§ 14.10 restricts only Customer: IBM is left free to assign the Agreement without our consent (and without any competitor bar), so the fallback elements of mutuality (both parties may assign to a successor; other assignments require consent, not unreasonably withheld) fail on their material terms. Our M&A carve-out is also narrower than the playbook (no Affiliate assignment and no sale of substantially all assets). No change-of-control provision exists, so we confirmed expressly that our change of control gives IBM no termination right. We therefore edited to the preferred position with two surgical changes, leaving the void-assignment and continuing-liability mechanics untouched.","proposal":"Make assignment reciprocal: Customer free to assign to Affiliates/successors; IBM assignment requires our consent and never to a competitor; no IBM termination right on our change of control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-311307de","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"No exclusivity, sole-source, requirements or \"shall not procure from third parties\" obligation is imposed on Customer anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for exclusivity, sole-supplier, minimum-commitment and non-compete language returned only (i) tax language (\"exclusive of any such taxes\"), (ii) the warranty disclaimer in § 5.2, and (iii) nonexclusive licence grants in §§ 5.4 and 12.1 — none of which restrict Customer's sourcing. § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively confirms that each party, including Customer, remains free to enter into similar agreements with others. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-1de5cfa0","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Other Disclaimers","rationale":"Section 7.0 Materials is the operative deliverables IP regime: Type I Materials vest title in Customer (§7.b), but Materials default to Type II if not specified, and for Type II IBM keeps all right, title and interest while our licence is limited to use/execute/reproduce/display/perform/distribute \\\"within Customer's Enterprise only\\\" — with no perpetual term, no modification right and no sublicensing, and §14.17 confirms no other licences are implied. That fails the fallback licence elements on material terms. Separately, §14.18 lets IBM and its Enterprise store and use our contact data anywhere they do business and pass it to contractors, Business Partners and assignees for promotions and marketing research, which is independent exploitation of Customer data rather than processing to provide the Services. We therefore target the fallback: we leave IBM's ownership of Type II (generic/pre-existing) Materials intact, broaden our deliverables licence, and confine IBM's data licence to providing the Services. We have not disturbed the Type I licence back in §7.b, which is outside this checklist.","proposal":"Broaden Type II Materials licence to perpetual, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense for Customer's business and limit IBM's use of Customer data to providing the Services.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2b274eef","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.1 License","rationale":"The operative Base Components grant in § 12.1 is expressly \"revocable\" and runs to \"Customer\" only (defined as Bluefly, Inc.), with § 14.17 confirming no other licences or rights are granted, so our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf have no coverage and no path to be added. That fails the fallback (affiliates covered) and sits in walk-away territory (revocable at Vendor's discretion with affiliates/contractors excluded). Two elements are already satisfied: § 7.0(c) grants an irrevocable paid-up licence for Type II Materials, and § 14.10 permits assignment of the Agreement to an M&A successor. We therefore delete the at-will revocability, extend the § 12.1 licence to Affiliates and contractors, tie termination to uncured material breach, and add \"perpetual\" to the paid-up Type II licence.","proposal":"Make the Base Components licence extend to Customer's Affiliates and contractors, terminable only for uncured material breach, and confirm the paid-up Type II licence is perpetual.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-ab397129","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Bluefly. Searches for \"compet*\", \"exclusive\", \"Customer shall not / may not\", field-of-use, territory and sole-source language return nothing binding our business: § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively preserves each party's freedom to enter into similar agreements with others; § 14.19 (Geographic Scope) limits only IBM's delivery obligations; § 14.17 and § 12.1 are ordinary licence-scope provisions (nonexclusive licence to use the Base Components in connection with the Services, plus standard no-reverse-engineering wording). § 14.11 (No Resale) bars only resale of IBM's own Services — a licence scope limit, not a restriction on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, and it leaves us free to procure, develop or acquire competing or alternative services. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-54ffa9fd","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11.3 Suspected Violations","rationale":"Subsection 11.3 is the only verification/investigation right binding Customer (there is no separate audit clause; searches for audit, inspection, records and verification return nothing else). It lets IBM investigate Customer's use of the Services and Content for AUP compliance with no frequency cap, no advance notice of the investigation itself (the notice in p0137 applies only before IBM restricts access or removes Content), and no cost allocation, while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over all relevant information on request. Unlimited and unannounced verification is walk-away territory and fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost, so we added the three fallback limits by the shortest insertion rather than rewriting the clause. Preferred extras (independent auditor, off-site, 5% threshold, no system access) are not pursued at this level.","proposal":"Add frequency, notice and cost limits to IBM's investigation right in 11.3","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-b39f640d","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.3 Choice of Law","rationale":"Section 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which is our preferred governing law, but the Agreement contains no venue, forum, or dispute-resolution provision anywhere (no arbitration clause either — searches for jurisdiction, venue, court and dispute return only unrelated indemnity/severability references). Without an exclusive forum, IBM could sue us in any competent court, so the clause fails the venue half of both the preferred and fallback positions. We added a single sentence fixing exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, with a customary carve-out for temporary injunctive relief, leaving the governing-law sentence untouched.","proposal":"Add exclusive New York County forum to the Choice of Law clause","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-a973d4af","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 3.4 Termination for Convenience","rationale":"Section 3.4(b) makes Customer's convenience termination conditional on paying \"early termination charges\" whose amount is left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments (no Attachment A charge schedule appears in the document), and Section 3.3 confirms those charges are recoverable by IBM except where IBM is the breaching party. That is an uncapped, Customer-payable liquidated amount, which fails the fallback requirement of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. We therefore adopted the fallback: a cap of three months' charges for the terminated Services, expressed as the sole liquidated amount payable by us, rather than deleting the charge outright (which would leave the Section 3.3 cross-reference dangling). The late payment fees referenced in Section 4.2 are a payment-timing charge rather than a liquidated damages regime and are noted only for completeness.","proposal":"Cap Section 3.4(b) early termination charges at three months' charges as the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-e3b3eff6","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.16 Freedom of Action","rationale":"The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation, best-price, most-favoured-customer, or right-to-match undertaking in either direction. Charges (§ 4.1) simply refer to Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, § 13.1 addresses only IBM's own price-change rights after twelve months, and Amendments (§ 13.3) requires mutual signature; targeted searches for most-favoured/favorable terms, best price, third-party offers, benchmarking and matching returned nothing. § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively confirms each party may enter similar agreements with others, so Bluefly is under no obligation to extend IBM terms no less favourable than those given to any third party. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-86ddcdeb","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4.1 Charges","rationale":"No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-cap obligation appears anywhere in the Agreement. Charges under § 4.1 arise only for Services ordered under Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), and § 4.2 payment is against invoices for amounts due, so Customer pays only for what it orders or uses. § 11.5 (Capacity Planning) allocates capacity-planning responsibility to Customer but imposes no committed capacity or minimum volume. Customer also retains a monthly termination for convenience right under § 3.4 and a no-charge exit under § 13.1 if IBM changes prices or terms. This meets the preferred position; the placeholder for \"early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A\" in § 3.4(b) is a termination-charge point to be handled under the termination rule, not a minimum commitment, so we do not flag it here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-43f9ef8f","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.8 Personnel","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding Customer. § 14.8 (Personnel), the likely home of such a restriction, addresses only supervision, assignment and subcontracting of personnel, and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) confirms each party remains free to contract with others. Section 9 caps are mutual at twelve months of charges but contain **no carve-out for confidentiality breach, gross negligence or wilful misconduct**, and § 6 expressly subordinates confidentiality to §§ 5, 9 and 10.

Two rules are **missing** entirely: post-termination transition assistance, Content return and deletion (§ 3.5 addresses only accrued payment obligations), and any vendor insurance covenant — both material given that IBM hosts the environment and processes personal information on our behalf under § 14.18.

Two findings (**RENEWAL** and **T4C**) are marked *needs review* and did not pass verification; they should not be relied on or sent to IBM until re-verified against the executed text.

| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |

The following findings sit in, or approach, walk-away territory under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

We require deletion of at-will revocability, extension to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, termination only for uncured material breach, and confirmation that the § 7.0(c) paid-up Type II licence is perpetual.
2. **§ 11.3 — unlimited, unannounced investigation right (AUDIT, medium).** No frequency cap, no advance notice of the investigation itself, no cost allocation, coupled with an obligation to hand over all relevant information on request. We require the three fallback limits (frequency, notice, cost).
3. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE, low severity but structurally material).** IBM hosts the environment and processes personal information under § 14.18; a data-processing vendor carrying no insurance is walk-away. We require the preferred covenant as a new § 14.21, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback available.
4. **§ 5.1/§ 5.2/§ 5.4 — care-and-skill warranty only (WARRANTY, medium).** The bargain fails every fallback element and approaches walk-away; we require the inserted 90-day software / 30-day Services conformance warranty with repair, replacement and refund remedies, drafted inside § 5.1 so § 5.2's exclusivity preserves rather than swallows it.

1. **Re-verify RENEWAL (§ 3.2) and T4C (§ 3.4) before circulating.** Both failed verification. Once confirmed, our positions are a sixty (60) day non-renewal window with renewal charges capped at 105% of the prior term, and a convenience right exercisable at any time on thirty (30) days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid charges (fallback: an express three-month cap in § 3.4(b)).
2. **Issue the redline** on the eight deviations and two missing clauses, in the order of the walk-away list above, with the drafted inserts for § 3.5 (transition assistance, Content return within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, certified deletion) and new § 14.21 (insurance).
3. **Add the mutual carve-out as new § 9.3** for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. If accepted, we then pursue the preferred-level points noted under LOL-CAP (USD 1,000,000 cap floor, fraud and IP carve-outs, exclusion of our payment obligations, and § 9.1(c)(2)'s disclaimer of liability for loss of or damage to our records or data).
4. **Fix venue.** § 14.3 already selects New York law (our preference) but the Agreement has no forum or dispute-resolution clause; add exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County with a carve-out for temporary injunctive relief.
5. **Cap the exit charge.** Adopt the fallback in § 3.4(b) — three months' charges for the terminated Services as the sole liquidated amount payable by us — rather than deleting the charge, to avoid a dangling cross-reference in § 3.3. Confirm whether an Attachment A charge schedule exists; none appears in the document reviewed.
6. **Escalation triggers.** If IBM refuses the § 12.1, § 11.3, insurance or warranty positions, escalate before further concessions. Separately, if any Order Form term exceeds twelve months, escalate to fix renewal terms at twelve months. If the deal permits a further ask on indemnity (currently compliant), we would add IBM cover for breach of applicable law, vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and trim § 8.2(a)(3)."}
